title: ULP-resolved residual-term attribution across the B1 and B2 status boundaries
question: Across every representable binary64 groundwater head between each frozen G21L boundary pair, which final residual components and node-4 flux terms carry the pass/fail change, and is that change smooth within a fixed solver path or dominated by path switching?
enumeration_contract: Enumerate every binary64 value in the closed interval by repeated math.nextafter from the lower numeric endpoint toward the upper numeric endpoint.
Abort if more than 128 representable heads are required; do not thin or resample after observing outcomes.
At each head execute one fresh immutable-origin G21I-style prefix solve with frozen production tolerances, max_retries=0 and the interval-specific max_iterations.
Capture solver status, nonlinear iterations, cumulative backtracking, full four-component residual vector and the six already-rounded node-4 terms through the existing G21M research-build observer.
Do not cache across heads and do not publish candidates, accepted state or ledger entries.
attribution_contract: For B1 compute node-4 residual, storage, upper-flux and lower-flux sequences; zero sink/source/root terms must remain zero for this frozen case.
For B2 compute all four residual-component sequences and the total residual sequence.
Between successive heads compute exact binary64 value deltas for every captured quantity.
For each interval report the total endpoint delta and the fraction attributable to each captured component/term, using signed deltas.

Partition samples by the exact tuple (solver_status, nonlinear_iterations, cumulative_backtracking). Within each partition ordered by head, report monotonicity of the active residual metric and of the dominant attributed term.
Report every transition where the solver-path tuple changes and every transition where status changes without a path-tuple change.
No smoothing, regression threshold or post-hoc neighborhood selection is allowed.
prospective_classification: TERM_SMOOTH_WITHIN_PATH if, within every path tuple containing at least three ordered samples, the active residual metric and dominant term are monotone and all status changes occur at criterion crossings without a path-tuple change.
PATH_SWITCH_DOMINATED if at least one status transition coincides with a path-tuple change and the same-path subsets are individually monotone.
TERM_JAGGED_WITHIN_PATH if a same-path subset with at least three samples is nonmonotone in the active residual metric or dominant term.
MIXED if both path-switch and within-path jagged mechanisms are observed.
gates: G21M parent result and temporary observer contract reproduce.
Both closed intervals are exhaustively enumerated with <=128 binary64 heads.
Frozen endpoint solver/residual observations reproduce G21M.
No accepted-state, candidate or ledger mutation occurs.
All sample records and path transitions are persisted.
Classification follows the preregistered rules without rebinning.
pass_interpretation: PASS attributes the observed threshold crossings to captured term evolution and/or solver-path switching at binary64 head resolution. It does not admit production changes. If same-path behavior is orderly and path switches explain the islands, G21 solver forensics should close and the coupling line should return to endpoint/residual-based qualification.
fail_interpretation: Preserve any endpoint mismatch, observer mismatch, >128-point interval or unclassified behavior. Do not change the frozen heads or classification rules.
